newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-LUYENDYK WINS SECOND INDY 500 IN STRANGE FINISH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LUYENDYK WINS SECOND INDY 500 IN STRANGE FINISH.

text.p: In a last lap dash featuring a controversial restart, Arie Luyendyk of the Netherlands won the rain-delayed 81st running of the Indianapolis 500 on Tuesday.

Luyendyk, the 1990 winner, claimed the 200-lap race victory over Treadway Racing teammate Canadian Scott Goodyear. by a margin of half a second. The Dutchman had squeezed past Goodyear with seven laps to go.
The race, which had been washed out Sunday and suspended after only 15 laps were completed because of rain on Monday, was a competitive tussle throughout, though slowed by a series of cautions.
The 12th caution period of the day, on lap 199, set the stage for the finish.
Luyendyk led Goodyear when the yellow flag was displayed for Tony Stewart. Stewart was running in fourth place when he brushed the fourth turn wall. Stewart was able to continue.
The United States Auto Club, which sanctions and officiates the race, wanted to have the race completed under green flag conditions to insure a competitive race.

With one lap left, chief steward Keith Ward called for the resumption of the race. The flagman displayed both the green and white flags together, which indicated the restart of the race and indicating one lap to go.

But the signal lights on the track remained yellow. Goodyear said later he thought the race would finish under caution because of the lights, and that there was no indication the race was going to restart.
Said Luyendyk about the confused messages: "I thought, the hell, if they don't know what they're doing, then I'll just keep going."
Goodyear's puzzlement may have cost him.
"I thought we were going to finish under the yellow," Goodyear said. "That is the very lap when you want to be ready to get on the gas and we weren't.
"We didn't really have any indication on the radio that it was going green. I'm not sure we would have had enough to pass him there at the end anyway. I'm just disappointed."
The Dutchman, who led for 61 laps and had been among the fastest drivers at the Speedway during the month, said when he saw the green flag, "I pushed down one gear and took off."

Goodyear was affected by another yellow flag controversy at Indianapolis Motor Speedway in 1995 when he was penalised for passing the pace car under yellow flag conditions while leading the race. Officials stopped scoring him at lap 195, costing him a potential victory.
Fearful of a similar situation, Goodyear was uncertain as to what to do. "It was still yellow (on the track), and I wondered what would have happened if I would have passed him," Goodyear said.
In defending the outcome of the race, which featured competitive action throughout the field, chief steward Ward took responsibility for the error, but downplayed it.
"I don't think what happened had any outcome of the race," Ward said.
The race 19 lead changes and 13 cars finished.
Rookie Jeff Ward, who led 49 laps during the latter stage of the race took third place ahead of defending champion Buddy Lazier, who led twice for a total of seven laps.
Tony Stewart led 64 laps, the most by any driver. He led five times during the race, before finishing fifth.
When asked if this was a sweeter victory than his 1990 win, which set the record for fastest Indy 500, Luyendyk said, "Yeah, sure. That was so long ago."
Race restarts were a problem throughout the day.
Robby Gordon was involved in a scary moment as his car caught fire just after he passed Luyendyk for second place as the suspended race resumed at the start of the day.
Gordon jumped from the burning car and began rolling on the ground to extinguish fires. Gordon suffered burns on his right hand, right thigh and both wrists.
Jockeying for position during a restart contributed to a pileup on lap 23 which involved Eliseo Salazar, Mark Dismore, Roberto Guerrero and Steve Kinser.
Other than the restarts, the race itself featured few high-speed crashes and only one driver, Paul Durant, suffering injuries that required hospitalization.
Durant got tangled with rookie Billy Roe in turn three, and the cars skidded together and hit the wall hard. Durant was hospitalized with a fractured pelvis and a concussion.
